corpusA.note: the round-1 abstract/intro/results/conclusion reported the first row as 'dormant under every request'; the second and third are the inertness readings

corpusB.note: the round-1 abstract/intro/results/conclusion reported the first row as 'dormant under every request'; the second and third are the inertness readings

confirm_regex.note: plus_oracle_confirm reproduces the round-1 '+ confirmation path' numbers (confirm = risk_tier == 'high'); plus_regex_confirm is the defender-computable rule the method section describes

paired.note: cells counts (entry, request) pairs by arm; entry_level_sign aggregates requests within an entry first

rho0_limits.note: the Clopper-Pearson limit treats the 200 contexts as i.i.d. Bernoulli trials; they cluster by entry

corpusB_fpr.note: the observed held-out rate is a POPULATION rate over heterogeneous null entries; Prop. 2 bounds the per-entry rate for an entry with rho_e <= rho0, which the closures and detours are not

corpusB_null_entry_rates.significance_note: plug-in k/n > rho0 is an estimate; 'significant' is a one-sided exact binomial test of k_div out of n_used at rho0, p < 0.05

conformal_per_entry.population_fpr_guarantee: Pr[flag] <= (m+1-j)/(m+1) = 0.049 <= alpha under exchangeability with the calibration class mix
conformal_per_entry.note: split-conformal threshold on held-out null ENTRIES; the null count on those same entries is in-sample, so the held-out null rate is the leave-one-out count

disjoint_calibration.note: calibration streams have a fixed length different from the SPRT-stopped evaluation streams, so the two k/n statistics are not exactly exchangeable

corrected_arithmetic.correct_statement: the sum is 0.842: uninformative as a probability bound, but not above 1

corollary2_magnitudes.note: the Q_u bound holds for any p_out >= 0, since rho >= (1-lambda) * Q_u(phi) * p_in; only the reachability clause (Q_u + TV of future sessions) needs p_out = 0

tv_estimate.note: a random within-user split has no temporal shift, so its TV is pure plug-in bias; only the excess is attributable to shift

vs_nmax16_paired.note: matched pair on the same sleeper units and held-out nulls; the full-corpus n_max=16 J (19/120 at 4/40) is a different sleeper population

calls.note: measured agent calls in this invocation (CRN: baselines shared per user)

vs_nmax16_paired.note: matched pair on the same sleeper units and held-out nulls; the full-corpus n_max=16 J (19/120 at 4/40) is a different sleeper population

calls.note: measured agent calls in this invocation (CRN: baselines shared per user)

cost_per_write.note: one with-entry call per probed context; common random numbers act on the baseline calls only, while the with-entry calls move with the budget and the corpus

budget.note: the offline rho0 sweeps in analyze_rev/replay re-test streams that STOPPED at the original flag, so they are bounds; the n_max=40 rows here are measured

corpusB_request_cond.verdict: the class is satisfied by an in-pool probe, so its detection rate says nothing about a pool-aware attacker

in_pool_requests.note: phi_verified_hold is 0 by construction: no context can satisfy the full predicate under a pool request

vs_legit_nulls.note: all 20 legitimate nulls (incl. opening hours) at n_max=16; superseded by vs_closure_detour_matched

judge_robust.unit: test units: split condition halves excluded, so corpus B is 120 sleeper units / 90 benign / 90 legitimate, as in Table I
judge_robust.note: neutral prompt states the property without naming the generator's payload classes and without exempting closures or alternatives

hold_unverified.note: hold-arm probes whose full predicate evaluates false on the context

retrieval.note: the retriever indexes entry TEXT and scores it against the rendered context plus the request; p_out in the paper is measured under forced inclusion, which this block prices

headline_scoring.note: the resolved-target configuration recalibrates the null on the SAME rule (10/600 -> rho0 = 0.0175) and is the internally consistent pair; corpus B is scored this way throughout

units.note: test units = single entries + complete split pairs counted once (corpus A: 71 + 14 = 85, with one orphan condition-only half among the 100 entries; corpus B: 108 + 12 = 120).  The round-1 text called these 'action-bearing sleepers', which is a different quantity: every entry except a split condition half states an action.

by_channel.runtime_gate_false_intervention_note: sessions here are probe contexts drawn with probe requests, one entry in the store; with a single entry the gate intervenes iff X(c)=1, so only the false-intervention rate and its cost are informative
